A rate limiter decides, per request, who may go now.","headline":{"text":"Rate limiter = per-request gatekeeper","semantic":"concept"},"tags":["Checkout errors","Too much traffic"],"statCards":[{"value":"31%","label":"checkouts failed","sourceRef":"num-15"}],"source":"Post-incident report: checkout errors on 14 March 2025"},{"beatId":"beat2","narration":"So each checkout request carries a key. That key owns a token bucket: a size, a refill rate. Say a hundred tokens, refilling ten a second. Each request spends one.","headline":{"text":"Token bucket = refilling allowance","semantic":"concept"},"tags":["Allowance per key","One token per request"]},{"beatId":"beat3","narration":"Why not give each gateway node its own bucket? Say twenty-four nodes. A client spread across them gets twenty-four times its limit. One shared store holds the bucket; every node reads and writes it there.","headline":{"text":"Shared store = one bucket for all","semantic":"concept"},"tags":["One bucket","All nodes agree"]},{"beatId":"beat4","narration":"But the store reads the count, adds tokens, spends one, then writes it back. Every step must be indivisible. Two nodes that read the same count both see a token, and both let a request through.","headline":{"text":"Read, spend, write: one step","semantic":"decision"},"tags":["Shared count","Double admit"]},{"beatId":"beat5","narration":"What happens when the shared store gets slow? Each request pays a network trip. Say zero point four milliseconds at the median. At p ninety-nine, two point one milliseconds.","headline":{"text":"Every check pays a round trip","semantic":"problem"},"tags":["Network hop","Every request"],"statCards":[{"value":"2.1 ms","label":"p99 store round trip","sourceRef":"num-6"}],"source":"A field guide to token-bucket rate limiting"},{"beatId":"beat6","narration":"Then a routine failover moved the limiter's store to a replica in another zone. Store calls jumped from about one millisecond to eighty. That's past the store timeout, so every check counted as a failure.","headline":{"text":"Store latency blows past the timeout","semantic":"problem"},"tags":["Cross-zone move","Timeout tripped"],"statCards":[{"value":"80 ms","label":"store call after failover","sourceRef":"num-16"}],"source":"Post-incident report: checkout errors on 14 March 2025"},{"beatId":"beat7","narration":"So the limiter was set to fail open, letting uncounted requests through. Each instance applied the limit locally. Traffic to the payment provider reached roughly forty times its contract. Thirty-one percent of checkouts failed.","headline":{"text":"Fail open wiped the shared limit","semantic":"problem"},"tags":["Fail open","Local limits"],"source":"Larkspur Pay platform team incident report, 14 Mar 2025"},{"beatId":"beat8","narration":"The provider limiter fails closed, refusing what it cannot count. Fallback limits split by instance count, so together they stay in contract. The store timeout rose to a hundred and fifty milliseconds, past a cross-zone trip. That checkout is refused, not multiplied.","headline":{"text":"Fail closed, split the fallback","semantic":"resolution"},"tags":["Fail closed","Split fallback"],"statCards":[{"value":"150 ms","label":"store timeout after fix","sourceRef":"num-20"}],"source":"Larkspur Pay platform team incident report, 14 Mar 2025"}]}
